intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from legendary local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently using a street food map.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, browse the vibrant night market, release a lantern on the Thu Bon River, and feast on local specialties like Cao Lau and White Rose Dumplings from street stalls. The town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns every evening, offering a deeply cultural and atmospheric experience.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass between Da Nang and Hue, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic coastal mountain roads. Stop at the old French and American war bunkers at the summit for panoramic views of the coastline and jungle-covered mountains.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Sampan Boat & Local Market Experience
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, hopping on a traditional sampan boat through narrow waterways, visiting the Cai Rang floating market, tasting fresh tropical fruits, and stopping at local workshops producing rice paper and coconut candy. A vivid window into rural Vietnamese life.
experiences.location: Cai Rang, Can Tho, Mekong Delta

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Night Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the legendary backpacker hub of Ho Chi Minh City, where Bui Vien Street comes alive at night with street food stalls serving Banh Trang Nuong (Vietnamese pizza), fresh spring rolls, and bia hoi (draft beer). Soak up the electric atmosphere, meet fellow backpackers, and experience the chaotic energy of Vietnam's most famous party street on an ultra-low budget.
experiences.location: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao Backpacker District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive on Flight UA at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange budget transport (airport bus or shared shuttle) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. If hungry, grab a quick snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or street vendor near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a convenience store or nearby street food stall (~30,000–50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs. Download Google Maps offline and Grab app for cheap local transport. Target spend today: under $5 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. After a slow start, take a walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get oriented. Explore the immediate neighborhood, find a local café, and plan your day over a Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local market or town center closest to your resort. Browse street stalls, observe daily local life, and pick up any essentials. Visit a nearby temple or pagoda for a free cultural experience. Walk or take a Grab bike to keep costs low.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local night market or busy street food strip. Sample classic Vietnamese dishes and soak in the vibrant atmosphere. Watch the sunset from the beach before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì from a street cart near the hotel (~20,000–30,000 VND) with Vietnamese iced coffee (~15,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (rice plate restaurant) — rice, veggies, and protein for (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Night market street food spread — try bún bò, gỏi cuốn, and chè dessert (~80,000–120,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Get a local SIM card today at a phone shop — Viettel or Vietnamobile offer budget data plans for ~100,000 VND. Start a small daily expense journal to track your budget.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise beach walk — free and beautiful. Head to a local pho stall for a traditional breakfast. Then visit the nearest cultural landmark, such as a Cham tower, fishing village, or historical monument depending on your resort's location.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~80,000–150,000 VND/day) to explore the surrounding countryside or coastal roads. Visit a local fishing harbor to see boats come in and interact with fishermen. Explore any nearby rice paddies or rural villages on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area for sunset. Join locals at a beachside plastic-stool restaurant for fresh seafood grilled simply — ask for the daily catch to get the best price.

meals.breakfast: Phở bò or phở gà from a local pho shop (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Roadside bún thịt nướng (grilled pork noodles) from a street stall (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish or shrimp at a local beachside eatery (~100,000–150,000 VND including rice and veggies)

day_by_day.notes: Always negotiate motorbike rental prices. Wear sunscreen — April can be hot and sunny in Vietnam. Carry a refillable water bottle; bottled water is cheap (~5,000–10,000 VND) but staying hydrated is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Buddhist pagoda or temple in the morning when it's less crowded and cooler. Observe monks, light incense, and learn about Vietnamese Buddhist culture — entry is free at most pagodas. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees).
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a local cooking class or food tour if available in your area (~200,000–400,000 VND for budget options). Alternatively, spend the afternoon at a local market learning about Vietnamese ingredients and trying tropical fruits like dragon fruit, rambutan, and jackfruit.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the old quarter or town center if nearby. Look for a bia hơi (fresh beer) spot — Vietnam's famous street-side draft beer culture where a glass costs as little as 5,000–10,000 VND. Great place to meet other backpackers and locals.

meals.breakfast: Xôi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor (~25,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) at a local restaurant (~45,000–65,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bia hơi street corner — order small plates of snacks like đậu phụ chiên (fried tofu), lạc rang (roasted peanuts), and nem (~60,000–100,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Bargain respectfully at markets — start at 50% of the asking price and meet in the middle. Avoid tourist-trap restaurants near major landmarks; walk one or two streets back for better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip planning day. Take a local bus or shared minivan to the nearest major town or city (use Grab or ask your hostel for the cheapest option). Arrive and explore the main attractions on foot — walking is free and the best way to discover hidden gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local history museum or cultural center (~20,000–40,000 VND entry). Explore the old town area, French colonial architecture, or any UNESCO-listed sites in the region. Take photos and journal your experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in the city before heading back to your resort. Explore any evening street food markets or night bazaars before catching transport back.

meals.breakfast: Bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) at a local eatery near the resort (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Mì Quảng or local regional noodle specialty at a city restaurant (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner in the city — bún chả or nem cuốn with a fresh coconut (~80,000–100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Check local bus schedules the night before. Shared minivans (xe khách) are often cheaper than tourist shuttles. Keep a photocopy of your passport when exploring new areas.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — swim, relax, and enjoy the natural beauty of Vietnam's coastline. This is a free activity and a great way to recharge mid-trip. Bring snacks from a convenience store to avoid overpriced beach vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby nature area — mangrove forest, lagoon, or national park if accessible from your resort. Many natural areas have free or very low-cost entry. Hire a local boat for a short lagoon tour (~100,000–150,000 VND shared).
day_by_day.evening: Cook or semi-cook your own meal — visit the local market, buy fresh ingredients, and use the hostel kitchen if available. This is a great budget hack and a fun cultural experience. Alternatively, find a family-run quán ăn (local eatery) for home-cooked Vietnamese food.

meals.breakfast: Cháo (rice porridge) with egg and ginger from a street stall (~30,000–45,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from the market — fresh fruit, bánh mì, and coconut water (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Home-cooked meal from market ingredients or family quán ăn (~60,000–90,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip is a good time to do laundry — most guesthouses offer laundry service for ~20,000–30,000 VND per kg, much cheaper than tourist laundromats.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local craft village or artisan workshop if nearby — lacquerware, silk weaving, pottery, or conical hat making. Many are free to observe and offer insight into Vietnamese craftsmanship. This is a deeply cultural experience with no tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Street food deep-dive afternoon. Make it a mission to try 5 different street foods you haven't eaten yet. Walk through residential neighborhoods and follow the locals to find the best hidden stalls. Try chè (sweet dessert soup), bánh xèo (sizzling pancake), or hủ tiếu.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at a scenic viewpoint — hilltop, lighthouse, or pier depending on your location. Bring a cold beer from a convenience store (~15,000–25,000 VND) and enjoy the view for free.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì ốp la (bánh mì with fried egg) (~25,000–35,000 VND) with cà phê đen (black coffee)
meals.lunch: Bánh xèo (sizzling Vietnamese pancake) at a street stall (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bún bò Huế (spicy beef noodle soup) at a local restaurant (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Take a free walking tour if available in your area — many cities offer volunteer-led tours where you tip what you can. Great for meeting fellow backpackers and learning history.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a local fish market or wet market (most active 5–8 AM). Watch the daily commerce, photograph the colorful produce, and experience authentic Vietnamese daily life. Grab breakfast from a market vendor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore any nearby islands, sand dunes, or natural landmarks via local transport. Vietnam's geography is incredibly diverse — ask your hotel about the most accessible natural wonder nearby. Many can be reached cheaply by local bus or shared boat.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner tonight — a mid-range local restaurant where you can try a multi-dish Vietnamese meal with soup, main, and sides. Still budget-friendly at under $8–10 USD per person.

meals.breakfast: Fresh market breakfast — bowl of bún riêu (crab noodle soup) from a market vendor (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cơm chiên (fried rice) with vegetables from a roadside stall (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Set meal at a local Vietnamese restaurant — canh chua (sour soup), cá kho tộ (braised fish), steamed rice (~150,000–200,000 VND for two dishes and rice)

day_by_day.notes: Check if there are any local festivals or events happening — Vietnam has numerous regional festivals that are free to attend and incredibly memorable for cultural travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Final full exploration day. Revisit your favorite spot from the trip — beach, pagoda, market, or viewpoint. Take time to reflect, journal, and buy any last-minute souvenirs. Best budget souvenirs: locally made snacks, instant Vietnamese coffee packs, and handmade crafts from local markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Slow afternoon — relax at the beach or pool, chat with fellow travelers, and compile your food and travel notes. Try any street food you missed during the trip. Visit a local café for a Vietnamese egg coffee (cà phê trứng) if available in your area.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — celebrate your Vietnam adventure with a spread of your favorite dishes from the trip. Head to your favorite street food spot or local restaurant. Toast with a bia hơi or fresh sugarcane juice.

meals.breakfast: Phở with extra herbs and chili — your last classic Vietnamese breakfast (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bánh mì with all the fillings — the ultimate Vietnamese sandwich (~25,000–40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Farewell feast at a local restaurant or street food market — order 3–4 shared dishes (~150,000–200,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Pack tonight to avoid morning stress. Keep essential documents, valuables, and a change of clothes in your carry-on. Check your flight details and arrange airport transport in advance — book a Grab or confirm a hotel shuttle.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a final Vietnamese breakfast near the hotel. Take one last walk on the beach or through the neighborhood to say goodbye. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport departure. Browse duty-free for last-minute gifts (Vietnamese coffee and cashews are great options). Reflect on 10 incredible days of street food, culture, and backpacking across Vietnam.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry local snacks for the journey — Vietnamese rice crackers and dried fruit make great airplane snacks.

meals.breakfast: Final street food breakfast near the hotel — cháo or bánh mì (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport food or packed snacks from a convenience store (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated daily budget: $20–35 USD per day covering accommodation (if splitting), food, transport, and activities. Vietnam is one of Southeast Asia's most rewarding budget destinations — your money goes far when you eat local and travel like a backpacker. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On flight or airport
meals.lunch: On flight or airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or hotel room service upon arrival — try instant pho or bánh mì if available locally

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm your hotel transfer in advance. Exchange some cash to Vietnamese Dong (VND) at the airport for small expenses. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Enjoy the coastal scenery and breathe in the sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local market or town center on foot or by xe ôm (motorbike taxi). Browse local stalls, pick up any travel essentials, and start soaking in Vietnamese street culture. Visit a nearby pagoda or cultural landmark for your first taste of Vietnamese heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the local waterfront or night market area. Watch locals gather for evening activities — a quintessential Vietnamese experience. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere as the town comes alive after sunset.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try cà phê trứng (egg coffee) or cà phê sữa đá (iced milk coffee) with bánh mì
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (everyday rice) restaurant near the resort — choose from pre-cooked dishes displayed at the counter, budget ~50,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood restaurant near the resort — grilled prawns, clams in lemongrass, and steamed fish with rice, budget ~150,000–250,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today. Your body is still adjusting to the time zone. Hydrate well — Vietnam can be hot and humid in April. Download Google Translate with Vietnamese offline for easy communication.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk or jog along the beach. Then head out to explore a local fishing village nearby — watch fishermen bring in their morning catch and interact with the community. A great authentic cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby historical or cultural site — a local museum, ancient temple complex, or heritage neighborhood depending on your resort's location. Hire a local guide for deeper cultural context (~200,000–300,000 VND for 2–3 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food walking tour or self-guided street food crawl through the local town. Sample multiple dishes from different vendors to maximize variety and flavor.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì from a street cart (~20,000–30,000 VND) with fresh-squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Bún bò Huế (spicy beef noodle soup) or local regional noodle specialty at a hole-in-the-wall restaurant — ~50,000–70,000 VND
meals.dinner: Street food crawl — try nem (spring rolls), bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), and grilled skewers from different vendors, budget ~100,000–150,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Carry small bills for street food vendors. Always look both ways before crossing the street — Vietnamese traffic can be chaotic but has its own rhythm!

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day cooking class at a local culinary school or family-run kitchen. Learn to make 3–4 classic Vietnamese dishes including pho or bánh xèo. This is a hands-on cultural and culinary experience (~400,000–600,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby craft village or artisan workshop — lacquerware, silk weaving, or pottery depending on the region. Watch artisans at work and pick up a small handmade souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show or folk music performance if available in the area. This is a uniquely Vietnamese art form dating back to the 11th century.

meals.breakfast: Phở bò (beef pho) at a local pho shop — the classic Vietnamese breakfast, ~50,000–70,000 VND
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you cooked in your morning cooking class — included in the class fee
meals.dinner: Vietnamese hotpot (lẩu) restaurant — great for a communal, interactive dining experience, ~150,000–200,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class a day in advance. Bring a reusable bag for market shopping during the class. The water puppet show usually has evening performances — check local listings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip excursion: Head to a nearby natural attraction — a national park, waterfall, cave system, or rice terrace depending on your location. Hire a local guide or join a small group tour (~300,000–500,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the day trip — explore hiking trails, boat rides, or scenic viewpoints. Take plenty of photos and interact with ethnic minority communities if in a highland area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Wind down with a traditional Vietnamese massage at a local spa (~200,000–300,000 VND for 60 minutes) to relieve any travel fatigue.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — buffet or set menu
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from a local bakery or eat at a rustic restaurant near the day trip site — try cơm lam (bamboo rice) if in a highland region
meals.dinner: Return to a favorite local restaurant from earlier in the trip, or try a new Vietnamese restaurant specializing in regional cuisine, ~100,000–180,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Start early for the day trip to avoid midday heat. Bring sunscreen, a hat, insect repellent, and a refillable water bottle. Wear layers if visiting highland areas.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike and explore the surrounding countryside at your own pace. Ride through local villages, rice paddies, and rural landscapes for an immersive backpacker experience (~50,000–150,000 VND/day rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a local family home for a homestay lunch experience if available, or visit a rural market. Explore a Buddhist pagoda or Cham tower if in central Vietnam. Take time to sit, observe, and journal.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and explore the local bar street or riverside promenade. Join other travelers at a backpacker-friendly bar for bia hơi (fresh draft beer, ~10,000–15,000 VND per glass) and good conversation.

meals.breakfast: Cháo (Vietnamese rice porridge) with shredded chicken at a local breakfast stall — ~30,000–50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Homestay lunch or local com tam (broken rice) restaurant with grilled pork, egg, and pickled vegetables — ~60,000–90,000 VND
meals.dinner: Bia hơi corner — order small plates of nhậu (drinking snacks) like fried tofu, grilled corn, and peanuts alongside cold draft beer — ~80,000–120,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Get an international driving permit if riding a motorbike. Always wear a helmet — it is the law and essential for safety. Bia hơi corners are a beloved Vietnamese social institution — embrace the experience!

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local morning market at dawn (around 5:30–7:00 AM) to see the full bustle of daily Vietnamese commerce — fresh produce, live seafood, herbs, and street food. Photograph the colorful chaos and chat with vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the beach near the resort. Swim, relax, read, or try water sports like kayaking or paddleboarding if available. This is your mid-trip recharge day.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar or beachfront lounge near the resort. Watch the sky turn golden over the water before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) or xôi (sticky rice) bought fresh from market vendors — ~25,000–40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch — fresh coconut, fruit platter, and a banh mi from a beach vendor
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual Vietnamese restaurant for a slightly elevated dinner — try chả cá (turmeric fish with dill) or bò lúc lắc (shaking beef), ~200,000–300,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: The morning market experience is best before 7 AM — go early! Apply reef-safe sunscreen at the beach. This is a good day to do laundry at a local laundromat (~30,000–50,000 VND/kg).

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip to a nearby island, bay, or river delta. Options may include snorkeling, visiting floating villages, or exploring mangrove forests by kayak. Book through a reputable local tour operator (~300,000–600,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat excursion or return and visit a local museum — history museum, war remnants museum, or ethnology museum to deepen your understanding of Vietnamese culture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local festival, street performance, or community event if one is happening. Check with hotel staff for local events. Otherwise, do a final deep-dive street food crawl through a neighborhood you haven't explored yet.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab bánh tiêu (hollow sesame donuts) and soy milk from a street cart
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch on the boat or island — freshly caught fish, crab, and shellfish cooked simply, often included in tour or ~100,000–150,000 VND extra
meals.dinner: Mì Quảng (Quang-style noodles) or regional specialty you haven't tried yet at a local restaurant — ~60,000–100,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Bring motion sickness tablets if you're prone to seasickness on boat trips. Waterproof your electronics in a dry bag. Check if the museum requires advance booking or has limited hours.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for personal exploration, last-minute souvenir shopping, or revisiting a favorite spot. Local markets are great for lacquerware, silk scarves, conical hats (nón lá), and Vietnamese coffee beans as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cyclo (three-wheeled bicycle rickshaw) tour through the old town or historic quarter if available — a leisurely, nostalgic way to see the city from a different perspective. Visit any remaining cultural sites on your list.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip, or splurge slightly at a well-regarded Vietnamese restaurant for a memorable final meal. Reflect on the journey over a glass of rượu (Vietnamese rice wine).

meals.breakfast: Revisit your favorite breakfast spot from the trip — a sentimental send-off meal
meals.lunch: Bún chả (grilled pork with rice noodles and herb plate) — a Vietnamese classic, ~60,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — order a spread of your favorite dishes from the trip: spring rolls, pho, seafood, and finish with chè (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup), ~200,000–350,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Vacuum-sealed Vietnamese coffee and dried foods make great carry-on souvenirs. Confirm your departure transfer and flight details tonight. Pack any fragile souvenirs carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise walk on the beach or a quiet café sit with a last cà phê sữa đá. Soak in the atmosphere one final time. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and settle any remaining bills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to the airport based on your flight schedule. Allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and immigration. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Vietnamese treats.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Carry fond memories, a full travel journal, and a deep appreciation for Vietnam's incredible food, culture, and people.

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast — a bowl of pho or bánh mì with iced coffee at a local café near the hotel before checkout
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or lounge — try to find a Vietnamese option even at the airport for one last taste
meals.dinner: On flight or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Keep all receipts for customs if you purchased high-value items. Ensure your passport, boarding pass, and travel documents are easily accessible. Leave a review for Aegean Bliss Resort and any outstanding local guides or tour operators who made your trip special!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in-flight or transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at 22:30 via Flight UA. Private airport transfer arranged by the resort. Enjoy a welcome drink and light late-night snack prepared by the resort upon arrival. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome snack platter and herbal tea arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort upon check-in

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your resort has a 24-hour concierge for smooth late-night check-in. Request a turndown service and early morning wake-up call if needed. Unpack essentials only and prioritize rest.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely sunrise on your private beachfront terrace. After breakfast, take a guided orientation walk of the resort grounds and surrounding coastal area. Arrange a private session with the resort's cultural guide to get a primer on Vietnamese customs, etiquette, and language basics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local village on a curated 'street food and culture' walking tour arranged by the resort concierge. Visit a local market to observe fresh produce, herbs, and spices used in Vietnamese cuisine. Try fresh coconut water and seasonal tropical fruits from market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar. Enjoy a premium multi-course Vietnamese tasting dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring locally sourced seafood and traditional recipes elevated with modern technique.

meals.breakfast: Full Vietnamese and international breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — phở, bánh mì, tropical fruits, freshly brewed Vietnamese egg coffee
meals.lunch: Street food tasting at the local village market — fresh spring rolls, bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), and grilled skewers with dipping sauces
meals.dinner: Premium multi-course tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — highlights include chilled prawn salad, steamed sea bass in ginger broth, and mango sticky rice dessert

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may still be a factor — keep the day relaxed and avoid overcommitting to activities. Stay hydrated and use reef-safe sunscreen if spending time on the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise kayaking session along the coastline with a certified guide. Explore hidden coves and sea caves only accessible by water. Return to the resort for a rejuvenating spa treatment — choose from a traditional Vietnamese herbal massage or a hot stone therapy session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day cultural excursion to a nearby historic pagoda or Cham temple complex. A knowledgeable local historian guide will provide in-depth context on Vietnamese spiritual traditions and architectural heritage. Browse artisan workshops for handcrafted lacquerware and silk products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private beach bonfire dinner setup. Enjoy freshly caught grilled seafood under the stars with curated Vietnamese wine and craft cocktails. Live acoustic Vietnamese folk music performed by a local duo.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-activity snack — Vietnamese rice porridge (cháo) with ginger and green onion, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Authentic lunch at a family-run restaurant near the temple — cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork), fresh herb salad, and iced lemon tea
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire seafood dinner — whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, clams in lemongrass broth, and bánh mì bruschetta with premium Vietnamese craft beer and cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly with covered shoulders and knees when visiting religious sites. Bring a light scarf or shawl. Confirm bonfire dinner setup with the resort concierge by midday.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered speedboat excursion to a secluded island or sandbar offshore. Snorkeling in crystal-clear waters with a marine guide — observe vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish. Enjoy a chilled champagne and fresh fruit spread on the boat deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the mainland and transfer to a premium cooking class hosted by a renowned local chef. Learn to prepare 4–5 iconic Vietnamese dishes including phở broth, fresh rice paper rolls, and caramelized clay pot fish (cá kho tộ). Take home a personalized recipe booklet.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a curated upscale local restaurant renowned for its fusion of traditional Vietnamese flavors and contemporary presentation. Opt for a chef's tasting menu with wine pairing. After dinner, stroll along the illuminated waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast in-room with Vietnamese cold brew coffee and fresh papaya with lime
meals.lunch: Champagne and canapés on the boat — smoked salmon, fresh oysters, tropical fruits, and Vietnamese rice crackers with prawn paste
meals.dinner: Chef's tasting menu at a premium local restaurant — highlights: crispy soft-shell crab, wagyu beef phở, lotus seed dessert with coconut cream, paired with curated Vietnamese and international wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and boat charter at least 24 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Bring waterproof bags for electronics during the boat excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided cycling tour through nearby rice paddies, villages, and rural landscapes. Stop at a local farm to learn about traditional Vietnamese agriculture — rice cultivation, herb gardens, and water buffalo farming. Engage with local farmers and try freshly harvested produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium silk weaving cooperative or artisan craft village. Participate in a hands-on workshop — try your hand at traditional silk weaving or hand-painting lacquerware under the guidance of a master artisan. Select premium handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Elevated street food experience — the resort arranges a private 'premium street food safari' with a culinary guide who navigates the best local stalls and hidden eateries. Sample an array of authentic Vietnamese street dishes in a curated, comfortable setting.

meals.breakfast: Vietnamese breakfast set at the resort — xôi (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots), soft-boiled eggs, fresh fruit platter, Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at a countryside homestay near the rice paddies — vegetable stir-fry, steamed rice, grilled river fish, and fresh herbs from the garden
meals.dinner: Premium street food safari — bún bò Huế (spicy beef noodle soup), bánh căn (mini rice cakes with quail eggs), chè (sweet dessert soup), grilled corn with scallion oil, and freshly squeezed sugarcane juice

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes for cycling and village walks. Bring insect repellent for the rice paddy areas. The street food safari is a curated experience — all vendors are vetted for hygiene and quality by the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium excursion to a UNESCO World Heritage Site or iconic Vietnamese cultural landmark (e.g., Hội An Ancient Town, Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary, or Huế Imperial Citadel depending on resort location). Depart early with a private air-conditioned vehicle and expert historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the heritage site — wander through ancient streets, merchant houses, and centuries-old temples. Participate in a traditional lantern-making workshop in Hội An or a royal court music performance in Huế. Browse premium boutiques for hand-embroidered silk and bespoke tailoring.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a rooftop or riverside restaurant in the heritage town. Immerse yourself in the magical ambiance of lantern-lit streets after dark. Return to the resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast box prepared by the resort — croissant, hard-boiled eggs, fresh fruit, Vietnamese drip coffee thermos
meals.lunch: Signature lunch at a heritage restaurant in the UNESCO town — Hội An white rose dumplings, cao lầu noodles, and crispy bánh bao vạc, with fresh limeade
meals.dinner: Riverside fine dining at a premium heritage restaurant — slow-braised duck with star anise, lotus root salad, steamed glutinous rice in banana leaf, and Vietnamese iced dessert, paired with premium local wine

day_by_day.notes: Start early to avoid midday heat and tourist crowds at heritage sites. Wear light, breathable clothing. The bespoke tailor shops in Hội An can produce custom garments in 24–48 hours if ordered today.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation day at the resort. Begin with a private beachfront yoga and meditation session at sunrise led by a certified instructor. Follow with a full-body traditional Vietnamese herbal wrap and aromatherapy treatment at the resort spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the resort's private beach and infinity pool at your leisure. Optional: arrange a private paddleboarding or stand-up surfing lesson with the resort's water sports team. Sip on fresh coconut water and tropical mocktails poolside.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-villa dining experience. The resort's executive chef prepares a bespoke 6-course Vietnamese degustation menu in your villa or on your private terrace. Paired with curated Vietnamese wines and artisanal craft cocktails. Enjoy a starlit evening with ambient music.

meals.breakfast: Spa-day wellness breakfast — açaí bowl, green smoothie, overnight oats with dragon fruit, herbal teas, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch — Vietnamese summer rolls with peanut dipping sauce, chilled prawn cocktail, avocado toast with pickled daikon, and fresh tropical fruit platter
meals.dinner: Private 6-course in-villa degustation — amuse-bouche of pho consommé shot, tuna tartare with Vietnamese herbs, lobster bisque with lemongrass foam, grilled wagyu with wok-fried morning glory, artisan cheese board, and mango panna cotta with passion fruit coulis

day_by_day.notes: This is a designated rest day — encourage relaxation and recovery. Pre-book the spa treatments and in-villa dining at least 48 hours in advance to ensure availability and personalization.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided excursion to a local fishing village at dawn. Join fishermen on a traditional wooden boat for a short fishing experience on the bay. Learn about traditional net-casting and fish trap techniques. Watch the morning catch being sorted and sold at the local fish market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to a premium eco-nature reserve or national park nearby for a guided jungle trek or mangrove kayaking experience. Spot native wildlife, exotic bird species, and tropical flora with a certified naturalist guide. Enjoy a picnic lunch in a scenic natural setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head to a premium rooftop bar or sky lounge for sundowner cocktails with panoramic coastal views. Enjoy a premium Vietnamese BBQ dinner at the resort's outdoor grill terrace — fresh seafood, premium meats, and vibrant salads.

meals.breakfast: Early morning fisherman's breakfast at the village — steaming bowl of bánh canh (thick noodle soup with fresh catch), fried dough sticks, and strong Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic in the nature reserve — artisan sandwiches, Vietnamese cold noodle salad, seasonal fruit, sparkling water, and premium Vietnamese iced tea
meals.dinner: Premium outdoor BBQ at the resort — whole grilled snapper with turmeric and dill, tiger prawn skewers with tamarind glaze, lemongrass chicken, grilled vegetables, and steamed jasmine rice, with craft cocktails and local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and light long-sleeve clothing for the nature reserve trek to protect against insects. Apply biodegradable insect repellent. Bring a waterproof camera or housing for the fishing boat experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter or seaplane scenic flight over the Vietnamese coastline, bay, and islands (subject to availability and weather). Alternatively, a premium chartered sunset cruise along the coast with snorkeling and cliff-jumping stops. A truly bucket-list aerial or nautical perspective of Vietnam's stunning geography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return and enjoy a premium Vietnamese coffee culture experience — visit a specialty Vietnamese coffee roastery and café. Learn about the history of Vietnamese coffee, from French colonial influence to modern third-wave culture. Taste a curated flight of Vietnamese coffees including egg coffee, coconut coffee, and single-origin pour-overs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cultural evening — attend a private traditional Vietnamese performing arts show featuring water puppetry, áo dài fashion showcase, and live đàn bầu (monochord) and đàn tranh (zither) music. Follow with a premium farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast at the resort before the morning excursion — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, Vietnamese pastries, tropical fruits, and sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the specialty coffee roastery — Vietnamese bánh mì with premium fillings, avocado salad, and a curated coffee flight pairing
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — 7-course tasting menu celebrating the best of Vietnamese regional cuisine, paired with fine wines and ending with a personalized dessert and farewell message from the chef

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter or seaplane experience well in advance — these are highly sought-after and weather-dependent. Confirm with the concierge 48 hours prior. The farewell dinner can be customized to dietary preferences upon prior request.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach or a gentle morning yoga session. Pack and prepare for departure. Visit the resort's boutique to pick up last-minute premium Vietnamese souvenirs — artisan coffee blends, handcrafted jewelry, silk scarves, and premium fish sauce gift sets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (negotiate with resort for extended checkout if flight allows). Enjoy one last leisurely lunch at the resort. Private transfer to the airport with the resort's luxury vehicle. Review and finalize any bespoke items ordered earlier in the trip (e.g., tailored clothing from Hội An).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Vietnam with extraordinary memories, a curated collection of souvenirs, and a deep appreciation for Vietnamese culture, cuisine, and natural beauty. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast at the resort — a personal favorite dish from the week, freshly brewed Vietnamese drip coffee, and a farewell tropical fruit platter
meals.lunch: Leisurely final lunch at the resort's poolside restaurant — Vietnamese noodle salad, fresh spring rolls, chilled coconut water, and a signature dessert
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium meal

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout at least 24 hours in advance. Confirm airport transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Keep all receipts for customs declarations if bringing back artisan goods or specialty food items. Ensure all tailored or custom items are collected before departure.
